extracted.intended_audience: public water systems (system operators), State regulators, and air carriers operating aircraft public water systems
extracted.subtask_description: EPA regulatory criteria for microbial treatment credits, integrity testing, monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping for public water systems (including a subpart for aircraft water systems). Covers membrane filtration, CT/UV/inactivation requirements, microbial toolbox reporting, sanitary survey response, and aircraft coliform sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: LRV_C-Test calculation for membrane challenge testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The removal efficiency of a membrane filtration process demonstrated during challenge testing must be expressed as a log removal value (LRV_C-Test). If fewer than 20 modules are tested, then LRV_C-Test is equal to the lowest of the representative LRVs among the modules tested. If 20 or more modules are tested, then LRV_C-Test is equal to the 10th percentile of the representative LRVs among the modules tested. The percentile is defined by (i/(n + 1)) where i is the rank of n individual data points ordered lowest to highest. If necessary, the 10th percentile may be calculated using linear interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control release value (QCRV) for membrane non-destructive test
rubrics_metrics.description: The challenge test must establish a quality control release value (QCRV) for a non-destructive performance test that demonstrates the Cryptosporidium removal capability of the membrane filtration module. This performance test must be applied to each production membrane module used by the system that was not directly challenge tested in order to verify Cryptosporidium removal capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production modules that do not meet the established QCRV are not eligible for the treatment credit demonstrated during the challenge test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-testing after membrane modification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a previously tested membrane is modified in a manner that could change the removal efficiency of the membrane or the applicability of the non-destructive performance test and associated QCRV, additional challenge testing to demonstrate the removal efficiency of, and determine a new QCRV for, the modified membrane must be conducted and submitted to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity testing definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct integrity test is defined as a physical test applied to a membrane unit in order to identify and isolate integrity breaches (i.e., one or more leaks that could result in contamination of the filtrate). Systems must conduct direct integrity testing in a manner that demonstrates a removal efficiency equal to or greater than the removal credit awarded to the membrane filtration process and meets the requirements described in paragraphs (b)(3)(i) through (vi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity testing applied to each membrane unit
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct integrity test must be independently applied to each membrane unit in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A membrane unit is defined as a group of membrane modules that share common valving that allows the unit to be isolated from the rest of the system for the purpose of integrity testing or other maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity method resolution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct integrity method must have a resolution of 3 micrometers or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution is defined as the size of the smallest integrity breach that contributes to a response from the direct integrity test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity test sensitivity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct integrity test must have a sensitivity sufficient to verify the log treatment credit awarded to the membrane filtration process by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitivity is defined as the maximum log removal value that can be reliably verified by a direct integrity test. Sensitivity must be determined using the approach in either paragraph (b)(3)(iii)(A) or (B) as applicable to the type of direct integrity test the system uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIT sensitivity calculation for pressure or vacuum tests (equation A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For direct integrity tests that use an applied pressure or vacuum, the direct integrity test sensitivity must be calculated according to the following equation: LRV_DIT = LOG10(Qp/(VCF × Qbreach)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where: LRV_DIT = the sensitivity of the direct integrity test; Qp = total design filtrate flow from the membrane unit; Qbreach = flow of water from an integrity breach associated with the smallest integrity test response that can be reliably measured; and VCF = volumetric concentration factor (ratio of suspended solids concentration on the high pressure side of the membrane relative to that in the feed water).

rubrics_metrics.name: DIT sensitivity calculation for particulate or molecular marker tests (equation B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For direct integrity tests that use a particulate or molecular marker, the direct integrity test sensitivity must be calculated according to the following equation: LRV_DIT = LOG10(Cf) − LOG10(Cp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where: LRV_DIT = the sensitivity of the direct integrity test; Cf = the typical feed concentration of the marker used in the test; and Cp = the filtrate concentration of the marker from an integral membrane unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a control limit within DIT sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must establish a control limit within the sensitivity limits of the direct integrity test that is indicative of an integral membrane unit capable of meeting the removal credit awarded by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when DIT exceeds control limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the result of a direct integrity test exceeds the control limit established under paragraph (b)(3)(iv) of this section, the system must remove the membrane unit from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must conduct a direct integrity test to verify any repairs, and may return the membrane unit to service only if the direct integrity test is within the established control limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct integrity testing frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct direct integrity testing on each membrane unit at a frequency of not less than once each day that the membrane unit is in operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may approve less frequent testing, based on demonstrated process reliability, the use of multiple barriers effective for Cryptosporidium, or reliable process safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect integrity monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct continuous indirect integrity monitoring on each membrane unit according to the criteria in paragraphs (b)(4)(i) through (v) of this section. Indirect integrity monitoring is defined as monitoring some aspect of filtrate water quality that is indicative of the removal of particulate matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system that implements continuous direct integrity testing in accordance with paragraphs (b)(3)(i) through (v) is not subject to continuous indirect integrity monitoring requirements. Systems must submit a monthly report summarizing all continuous indirect integrity monitoring results triggering direct integrity testing and the corrective action that was taken in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect monitoring must include filtrate turbidity (unless State approves alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the State approves an alternative parameter, continuous indirect integrity monitoring must include continuous filtrate turbidity monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect monitoring sampling frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous monitoring must be conducted at a frequency of no less than once every 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect monitoring must be conducted per membrane unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous monitoring must be separately conducted on each membrane unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity trigger for direct integrity testing
rubrics_metrics.description: If indirect integrity monitoring includes turbidity and if the filtrate turbidity readings are above 0.15 NTU for a period greater than 15 minutes (i.e., two consecutive 15-minute readings above 0.15 NTU), direct integrity testing must immediately be performed on the associated membrane unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-approved alternative indirect parameter trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: If indirect integrity monitoring includes a State-approved alternative parameter and if the alternative parameter exceeds a State-approved control limit for a period greater than 15 minutes, direct integrity testing must immediately be performed on the associated membrane units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly indirect monitoring reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must submit a monthly report to the State summarizing all continuous indirect integrity monitoring results triggering direct integrity testing and the corrective action that was taken in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second stage filtration 0.5-log Cryptosporidium credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive 0.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment credit for a separate second stage of filtration that consists of sand, dual media, GAC, or other fine grain media following granular media filtration if the State approves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, the first stage must be preceded by a coagulation step and both filtration stages must treat the entire plant flow taken from a surface water or GWUDI source. A cap, such as GAC, on a single stage of filtration is not eligible for this credit. The State must approve the treatment credit based on an assessment of the design characteristics of the filtration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow sand filtration as secondary filter 2.5-log credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems are eligible to receive 2.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment credit for a slow sand filtration process that follows a separate stage of filtration if both filtration stages treat entire plant flow taken from a surface water or GWUDI source and no disinfectant residual is present in the influent water to the slow sand filtration process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State must approve the treatment credit based on an assessment of the design characteristics of the filtration process. This paragraph does not apply to treatment credit awarded to slow sand filtration used as a primary filtration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: CT calculation (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: CT is the product of the disinfectant contact time (T, in minutes) and disinfectant concentration (C, in milligrams per liter). Systems with treatment credit for chlorine dioxide or ozone must calculate CT at least once each day, with both C and T measured during peak hourly flow as specified in §§ 141.74(a) through (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: CT addition across disinfection segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems with several disinfection segments in sequence may calculate CT for each segment (a segment = treatment unit process with measurable disinfectant residual and liquid volume) and must add the Cryptosporidium CT values in each segment to determine the total CT for the treatment plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine dioxide CT values and interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive the Cryptosporidium treatment credit listed in the chlorine dioxide CT table by meeting the corresponding chlorine dioxide CT value for the applicable water temperature. Systems may use the equation to determine log credit between indicated values: Log credit = (0.001506 × (1.09116)^Temp) × CT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CT values vary by log credit and water temperature (table provided in regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ozone CT values and interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive the Cryptosporidium treatment credit listed in the ozone CT table by meeting the corresponding ozone CT value for the applicable water temperature. Systems may use the equation to determine log credit between indicated values: Log credit = (0.0397 × (1.09757)^Temp) × CT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CT values vary by log credit and water temperature (table provided in regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: State approval of site-specific CT values
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may approve alternative chlorine dioxide or ozone CT values to those listed on a site-specific basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State must base this approval on a site-specific study a system conducts that follows a State-approved protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: UV dose table for treatment credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems receive Cryptosporidium, Giardia lamblia, and virus treatment credits for ultraviolet (UV) light reactors by achieving the corresponding UV dose values shown in the UV dose table for 254 nm low pressure mercury vapor lamps. To receive treatment credit for other lamp types, systems must demonstrate an equivalent germicidal dose through reactor validation testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UV dose values in the table are applicable only to post-filter applications of UV in filtered systems and to unfiltered systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: UV reactor validation testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use UV reactors that have undergone validation testing to determine the operating conditions under which the reactor delivers the UV dose required. These operating conditions must include flow rate, UV intensity as measured by a UV sensor, and UV lamp status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining validated operating conditions, systems must account for UV absorbance of the water; lamp fouling and aging; measurement uncertainty of on-line sensors; UV dose distributions arising from velocity profiles through the reactor; failure of UV lamps or other critical system components; and inlet and outlet piping or channel configurations. Validation testing must include full scale testing of a reactor that conforms uniformly to the UV reactors used by the system and inactivation of a test microorganism whose dose response characteristics have been quantified with a low pressure mercury vapor lamp. The State may approve an alternative approach to validation testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: UV reactor monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must monitor their UV reactors to determine if the reactors are operating within validated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring must include UV intensity as measured by a UV sensor, flow rate, lamp status, and other parameters the State designates. Systems must verify the calibration of UV sensors and must recalibrate sensors in accordance with a protocol the State approves.

rubrics_metrics.name: UV treatment credit operational threshold (95% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive treatment credit for UV light, systems must treat at least 95 percent of the water delivered to the public during each month by UV reactors operating within validated conditions for the required UV dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must demonstrate compliance with this condition by the monitoring required under the reactor monitoring provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reporting requirements (sampling, storage, bin classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report sampling schedules under § 141.702 and source water monitoring results under § 141.706 unless they notify the State that they will not conduct source water monitoring due to meeting the criteria of § 141.701(d). Systems must report the use of uncovered finished water storage facilities to the State. Filtered systems must report their Cryptosporidium bin classification. Unfiltered systems must report their mean source water Cryptosporidium level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must report disinfection profiles and benchmarks to the State as described in §§ 141.708 through 141.709 prior to making a significant change in disinfection practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microbial toolbox reporting or State certification alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report to the State in accordance with the provided table for any microbial toolbox options used to comply with treatment requirements under § 141.711 or § 141.712. Alternatively, the State may approve a system to certify operation within required parameters for treatment credit rather than reporting monthly operational data for toolbox options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watershed control program (WCP) reporting schedule and items
rubrics_metrics.description: For WCPs systems must submit: (i) Notice of intention to develop a new or continue an existing WCP no later than two years before the applicable treatment compliance date; (ii) Watershed control plan no later than one year before compliance date; (iii) Annual watershed control program status report every 12 months beginning one year after compliance date; (iv) Watershed sanitary survey report for community water systems every three years beginning three years after compliance date, and for noncommunity water systems every five years beginning five years after compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative source/intake management reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification that system has relocated the intake or adopted the intake withdrawal procedure reflected in monitoring results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit no later than the applicable treatment compliance date in § 141.713.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presedimentation monthly verification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification that: (i) Continuous basin operation; (ii) Treatment of 100% of the flow; (iii) Continuous addition of a coagulant; (iv) At least 0.5-log mean reduction of influent turbidity or compliance with alternative State-approved performance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage lime softening monthly verification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification that: (i) Chemical addition and hardness precipitation occurred in two separate and sequential softening stages prior to filtration; (ii) Both stages treated 100% of the plant flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank filtration demonstration and turbidity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial demonstration of: (A) Unconsolidated, predominantly sandy aquifer; (B) Setback distance of at least 25 ft. (0.5-log credit) or 50 ft. (1.0-log credit). Additionally, if monthly average of daily max turbidity is greater than 1 NTU then system must report result and submit an assessment of the cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial demonstration due no later than the applicable treatment compliance date. Turbidity exceedance report within 30 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined filter performance monthly verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification of combined filter effluent (CFE) turbidity levels less than or equal to 0.15 NTU in at least 95 percent of the 4 hour CFE measurements taken each month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual filter performance monthly verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification that: (i) Individual filter effluent (IFE) turbidity levels less than or equal to 0.15 NTU in at least 95 percent of samples each month in each filter; (ii) No individual filter greater than 0.3 NTU in two consecutive readings 15 minutes apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of performance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial submission: results from testing following a State approved protocol. Ongoing: as required by the State, monthly verification of operation within conditions of State approval for demonstration of performance credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial results due no later than the applicable treatment compliance date; monthly verification reporting within 10 days following the monitoring month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bag filters and cartridge filters reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration that: (A) Process meets the definition of bag or cartridge filtration; (B) Removal efficiency established through challenge testing that meets criteria in this subpart. Also monthly verification that 100% of plant flow was filtered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial demonstration due no later than the applicable treatment compliance date. Monthly verification reporting within 10 days following the month in which monitoring was conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membrane filtration reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial submission: Results of verification testing demonstrating: (A) Removal efficiency established through challenge testing that meets criteria in this subpart; (B) Integrity test method and parameters, including resolution, sensitivity, test frequency, control limits, and associated baseline. Ongoing: Monthly report summarizing: (A) All direct integrity tests above the control limit; (B) If applicable, any turbidity or alternative state-approved indirect integrity monitoring results triggering direct integrity testing and the corrective action that was taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial results due no later than the applicable treatment compliance date. Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which monitoring was conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second stage filtration reporting (monthly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification that 100% of flow was filtered through both stages and that first stage was preceded by coagulation step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow sand filtration (secondary) reporting (monthly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly verification that both a slow sand filter and a preceding separate stage of filtration treated 100% of flow from subpart H sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine dioxide CT reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of CT values for each day as described in § 141.720.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ozone CT reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of CT values for each day as described in § 141.720.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report within 10 days following the month in which the monitoring was conducted, beginning on the applicable treatment compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: UV validation and monthly reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Validation test results demonstrating operating conditions that achieve required UV dose must be submitted. (ii) Monthly report summarizing the percentage of water entering the distribution system that was not treated by UV reactors operating within validated conditions for the required dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation test results due no later than the applicable treatment compliance date. Monthly reporting within 10 days following the month in which monitoring was conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: source water monitoring retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must keep results from the initial round of source water monitoring under § 141.701(a) and the second round of source water monitoring under § 141.701(b) until 3 years after bin classification under § 141.710 for filtered systems or determination of the mean Cryptosporidium level under § 141.710 for unfiltered systems for the particular round of monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: notification to State retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must keep any notification to the State that they will not conduct source water monitoring due to meeting the criteria of § 141.701(d) for 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: treatment monitoring and uncovered finished water reservoirs
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must keep the results of treatment monitoring associated with microbial toolbox options under §§ 141.716 through 141.720 and with uncovered finished water reservoirs under § 141.714, as applicable, for 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary survey definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A sanitary survey is an onsite review of the water source (identifying sources of contamination by using results of source water assessments where available), facilities, equipment, operation, maintenance, and monitoring compliance of a PWS to evaluate the adequacy of the PWS, its sources and operations, and the distribution of safe drinking water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant deficiency definition (sanitary surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of this section, a significant deficiency includes a defect in design, operation, or maintenance, or a failure or malfunction of the sources, treatment, storage, or distribution system that EPA determines to be causing, or has the potential for causing the introduction of contamination into the water delivered to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to significant deficiencies identified by EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: For sanitary surveys performed by EPA, systems must respond in writing to significant deficiencies identified in sanitary survey reports no later than 45 days after receipt of the report, indicating how and on what schedule the system will address significant deficiencies noted in the survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must correct significant deficiencies according to the schedule approved by EPA, or if there is no approved schedule, according to the schedule reported under paragraph (c) if such deficiencies are within the control of the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft PW S applicability and compliance date
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of Subpart X constitute the National Primary Drinking Water Regulations for aircraft that are public water systems and that board only finished water for human consumption. Aircraft public water systems are considered transient non-community water systems (TNCWS). Aircraft public water systems must comply, unless otherwise noted, beginning October 19, 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent there is a conflict between requirements in this subpart and elsewhere in this part, this subpart governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft coliform sampling plan required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each air carrier must develop a coliform sampling plan covering each aircraft water system that identifies: (1) Coliform sample collection procedures consistent with § 141.803(a) and (b); (2) Sample tap location(s) representative of the aircraft water system as specified in § 141.803(b)(2) and (b)(4); (3) Frequency and number of routine coliform samples to be collected as specified in § 141.803(b)(3); (4) Frequency of routine disinfection and flushing as specified in the operations and maintenance plan under § 141.804; (5) Procedures for communicating sample results promptly so required actions will be conducted in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coliform sampling plan must be included in the Aircraft Water System Operations and Maintenance Plan required in § 141.804. Any subsequent changes must also be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to develop aircraft coliform sampling plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Each air carrier must develop a coliform sampling plan for each aircraft with a water system meeting the definition of a public water system by April 19, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methodology for aircraft coliform sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard sample volume required for total coliform analysis, regardless of analytical method used, is 100 mL. Air carriers need determine only the presence or absence of total coliforms and/or E. coli; a determination of density is not required. Air carriers must conduct analyses in accordance with the analytical methods specified in the regulation. The time from sample collection to initiation of analysis may not exceed 30 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invalidation of a total coliform sample result can be made only by the Administrator or by the certified laboratory in accordance with specified regulatory sections. For compliance, samples may be considered only if analyzed by a laboratory certified by a State or EPA (State refers to a State or Tribe with primacy under SDWA). Systems are encouraged but not required to hold samples below 10 °C during transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft routine monitoring frequency and sample counts
rubrics_metrics.description: For each aircraft water system, the sampling frequency must be determined by the disinfection and flushing frequency recommended by the aircraft water system manufacturer and as identified in the operations and maintenance plan. Except as provided, the air carrier must collect two 100 mL total coliform routine samples at the frequency specified in the sampling plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: the air carrier may collect one 100 mL routine sample for aircraft with a removable or portable tank drained every day of passenger service and only one tap. Air carriers must perform routine monitoring for total coliform at a frequency corresponding to the frequency of routine disinfection and flushing as specified in Table B-1. One sample must be taken from a lavatory and one from a galley; if only one tap exists then a single tap may be used to collect two separate 100 mL samples. Routine total coliform samples must not be collected within 72 hours after completing routine disinfection and flushing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft positive routine sample actions — E. coli-positive
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine sample is E. coli-positive, the air carrier must: (i) Restrict public access to the aircraft water system as expeditiously as possible, but in no case later than 24 hours after the laboratory notifies the air carrier of the E. coli-positive result; (ii) Disinfect and flush the system in accordance with § 141.804(b)(2). If the system cannot be physically disconnected or shut-off, disinfect and flush no later than 72 hours after notification; (iii) Collect follow-up samples in accordance with paragraph (e). A complete set of follow-up samples must be total coliform-negative before providing water for consumption and returning to routine monitoring frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All public access restrictions, including notification requirements, must remain in place until the system has been disinfected and flushed and follow-up samples are negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft positive routine sample actions — total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative
rubrics_metrics.description: If any routine sample is total coliform-positive and E. coli-negative, the air carrier must perform at least one of the following corrective actions and continue until a complete set of follow-up or repeat samples is total coliform-negative: (i) Disinfect and flush the system in accordance with § 141.804(b)(2) no later than 72 hours after notification and collect follow-up samples before providing water for consumption; (ii) Restrict public access in accordance with paragraph (d) as expeditiously as possible but no later than 72 hours after notification; (iii) Repeat sampling: collect three 100 mL repeat samples no later than 24 hours after notification from specified taps (the tap that was positive, one other lavatory tap, and one other galley tap).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all repeat samples are total coliform-negative, the air carrier must maintain the routine monitoring frequency. If any repeat sample is E. coli-positive, the air carrier must perform all corrective actions specified for an E. coli-positive result. (Further outcomes and requirements continue as specified in regulation.)
